assessment.nobel_worthiness: Turns ubiquitin-proteasome chemistry into a general design principle: a bifunctional or glue molecule hijacks an E3 ligase to destroy a chosen protein. This converts a biological process into a defined chemical tool and opens previously undruggable targets; clinical-stage molecules exist. Strong in originality and medical relevance.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept (2001) and Crews drove the field; Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explains the molecular-glue branch and enabled CRBN-based degraders. Ciulli, Gray and others made major later advances, so the three-person split is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Concept validated by many independent groups and a large clinical pipeline, though no PROTAC is yet an approved drug; timing is arguably slightly early but the chemistry is well established.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should recognise PROTACs, molecular glues, or both, and how to treat the thalidomide-CRBN work as separate from PROTAC design.
Absence of an approved PROTAC drug as a maturity test.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base into another (cytosine deamination, engineered adenosine deamination) at a programmed genomic site without double-strand breaks. A clean chemistry-of-nucleic-acids solution with direct consequences for genome maintenance research and therapy; very high impact.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu is the clear intellectual driver; Komor and Gaudelli were lead trainees who built the first cytosine and adenine editors. A fair prize could go to Liu alone or with the two first authors; the supplied credit also lists Kondo and Nishida for the independent Target-AID work.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly confirmed independently across organisms and already in clinical trials, with first patient benefit reported; recognition is timely though the field is young. Overlaps with the CRISPR prize of 2020 in enabling technology.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views base editing as sufficiently distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Allocation between Liu's lab members and the Kondo/Nishida group.
Long-term safety and off-target deamination profiles are still being characterised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminator chemistry transformed measurement of nucleic acids, including genome-wide analysis of replication, mutation and nucleotide incorporation. The enabling chemistry is concrete and the lasting impact on biology and medicine is enormous.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived and developed the Solexa chemistry and single-molecule approach; Mayer's colony/clonal amplification work is a decisive complementary contribution. Rothberg (pyrosequencing, 454) and Ju (reversible terminators) have competing claims, so credit is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Technology is thoroughly established and independently reproduced; if anything recognition is overdue, with the Sanger precedent already in Chemistry.
uncertainties: Priority between solid-phase clonal amplification, reversible terminators and pyrosequencing.
Whether sequencing platforms are viewed as chemistry or as technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the chemical delivery system that made siRNA and mRNA medicines work, including COVID-19 vaccines. The lipid pKa and formulation chemistry is a well-defined, original and highly consequential achievement.
assessment.attribution: Cullis, Hope and Madden at UBC established the pH-dependent ionizable lipid and rapid-mixing formulation principles; Anderson and Langer later optimised lipid libraries and MacLachlan contributed industrially. Credit is distributed and partly industrial, but a Cullis-centred trio is defensible.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale and independently reproduced; recognition is timely, especially after the 2023 Medicine prize for nucleoside modification.
uncertainties: Relation to the 2023 Medicine prize may make the committee see this as already honoured.
Patent and industry contributions complicate attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative mass-spectrometry proteomics lets cells be measured at the level of thousands of proteins and modifications, a measurement-based approach that has exposed regulatory mechanisms across biology. Importance is high and it is a general tool for biologists.
assessment.attribution: Mann (high-resolution, SILAC and proteome-wide quantification), Aebersold (targeted/SRM and SWATH, ICAT) and Yates (shotgun, MudPIT) are the leading figures; Gygi, Hunt and Heck also have strong claims, making a three-person selection arbitrary to some degree.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely adopted and independently validated; the ESI/MALDI prize of 2002 recognised ionisation, so a proteomics prize is a natural second step.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 Chemistry prize for MS biomolecule ionisation.
Many near-equal contributors, so the split is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery that m6A is a reversible, regulated RNA modification with writers, erasers and readers established an epitranscriptomic layer of chemistry controlling gene expression. Original and broadly consequential, linking a chemical modification to biological function.
assessment.attribution: Chuan He (FTO as demethylase, readers, chemical biology), Jaffrey (mapping, function) and the Rechavi/Dominissini mapping effort (m6A-seq) all made decisive contributions; Jia and others also credited, so allocation is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Strongly replicated at the level of enzymes and mapping, but quantitative stoichiometry, antibody specificity and some mapping results have been challenged; interpretation of function is still evolving, so slightly premature.
uncertainties: Reproducibility and specificity concerns in antibody-based mapping and in stoichiometry measurements.
Which functional claims of the pathway are settled.
Attribution among He, Jaffrey and Rechavi's groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structure and mechanism of nitrogenase explain how biology breaks the N2 triple bond, a central problem in the chemistry of life. Crystallography of the FeMo cofactor, the central carbide, and E4 intermediate mechanism are fundamental enzymology.
assessment.attribution: Rees and Einsle provided the crystal structures and the central light atom; Seefeldt and Dean contributed biochemistry and the Lowe-Thorneley-style mechanistic framework; Ribbe made cofactor assembly contributions. A fair prize is possible but must separate structure from mechanism.
assessment.maturity: Structures are reproduced across labs, though the complete catalytic cycle and the N2-binding intermediates remain debated, so mechanistic maturity is partial.
uncertainties: Catalytic mechanism and hydride-bridge intermediates are not fully resolved.
Allocation between structural and biochemical contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Activity-based protein profiling uses covalent probes to read out the functional state of enzymes directly in proteomes, converting enzymology into a general chemical-proteomic method. It supports target discovery and inhibitor selectivity, a clear chemical tool for biologists.
assessment.attribution: Cravatt is the principal originator and developer of the platform for serine hydrolases and beyond; Bogyo made important cysteine protease and imaging probes. Overkleeft and Weerapana added significant chemistries, so credit is shared but Cravatt's role is dominant.
assessment.maturity: Method widely adopted and independently confirmed, yielding clinical-stage compounds; recognition would be timely, though less foundational than competing biomedical candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the method's impact is judged transformative enough compared with other chemical-biology candidates.
Weighting of Bogyo versus other probe developers.
